P003-D001.title: Discharge letter after status asthmaticus
P003-D001.text:
Dear colleagues,
We report on the inpatient stay of Sabine Gruber, born 14.02.1993, from 01.04.2009 to 03.04.2009.

Reason for admission: status asthmaticus with known allergic bronchial asthma (since about age 7).
Previous treatment: budesonide inhaler and salbutamol as needed.

Inpatient treatment: salbutamol inhalations, systemic corticosteroids (prednisolone IV), oxygen. Rapid improvement.

Allergies: penicillin – confirmed allergy (urticaria after amoxicillin at age 5, documented by the GP). CAUTION penicillin allergy!
Family history: mother with bronchial asthma.

Discharged in good general condition. Continue the inhaler plan.
Diagnoses: allergic bronchial asthma (J45.0). Status asthmaticus (J46).
Kind regards, Senior Dr Petra Salzmann, paediatrics

P003-D002.title: Pulmonology check-up for asthma
P003-D002.text:
Patient Sabine Gruber, born 14.02.1993, female. Check-up for bronchial asthma.

History: asthma since childhood, recently well controlled on budesonide/formoterol (Symbicort Turbohaler 160/4.5 µg) twice daily and salbutamol as needed. Last asthma attack about 2 years ago (no admission).
Smoking: non-smoker.
Allergies: penicillin allergy (urticaria), documented.

Spirometry:
  FEV1: 82% predicted (slightly reduced)
  FEV1/FVC: 76% (mildly obstructive)
  Reversibility: FEV1 +14% after salbutamol → significant reversibility → asthma confirmed.

Assessment: bronchial asthma GINA step 3, moderate persistent, well controlled.
Recommendation: continue budesonide/formoterol twice daily, salbutamol spray as emergency medication. Check in 12 months.
Family history: mother also has asthma.
No other previous illnesses.

P003-D003.title: Emergency referral for acute lower abdominal pain
P003-D003.text:

P003-D004.title: Admission report, surgery – suspected appendicitis
P003-D004.text:
Admission: 08.07.2024, 22:30
Ward: surgery C-3
Patient: Gruber Sabine, born 14.02.1993, female

Referral diagnosis: suspected appendicitis

History:
Increasing pain in the right lower abdomen since about 18:00, NRS 6/10. Nausea without vomiting. Temp 37.9°C at home. Last meal about 17:00. Menstrual history: period 10 days ago, none now.

P003-D005.title: Nursing report, night of admission
P003-D005.text:

Inhaler: budesonide/formoterol given as ordered.
Emotional state: anxious about surgery, reassured.

P003-D007.title: Ultrasound abdomen/pelvis
P003-D007.text:
Report: ultrasound of the abdomen and pelvis, 09.07.2024, 00:15
Patient: Gruber Sabine, born 14.02.1993

Clinical question: suspected appendicitis. Gynaecological cause?

Findings:
Appendix: visible, outer diameter 9 mm, wall thickening, not compressible, surrounding increased echogenicity (local inflammation) → consistent with acute appendicitis.
No free gas. Small amount of free fluid around the appendix → early perforation cannot be safely excluded.
Ovaries: left ovary with a hypoechoic lesion about 2.5 cm, suspected follicular cyst. Right ovary: normal.
Uterus: normal.
Spleen, liver, kidneys: normal.

Assessment:
1. Acute appendicitis (appendix diameter 9 mm, wall thickening). Free fluid around the appendix – perforation possible, assess during surgery.
2. Lesion of the left ovary (hypoechoic, 2.5 cm) – most likely a follicular cyst, differential ovarian cyst. Gynaecological check after surgery recommended.
3. No sign of pancreatitis or urinary tract disease.

P003-D008.title: Senior doctor decision: surgery indicated, allergy note
P003-D008.text:
09.07.2024, 01:00, Senior Dr Franz Kern, general surgery

After reviewing ultrasound and lab: appendicitis confirmed, surgery indicated.
Free fluid around the appendix – early perforation cannot be excluded. Laparoscopic appendectomy planned tonight.

Nursing information received: the patient reports a penicillin allergy (urticaria after amoxicillin as a child). Admission report incorrect – it says "no known allergies". CAUTION: penicillin allergy documented and recorded in the patient file!

Anaesthesia informed (emergency, night).
Antibiotic prophylaxis: NO amoxicillin/clavulanic acid (penicillin allergy)! Alternative: metronidazole 500 mg IV and cefuroxime 1.5 g IV (cephalosporin – low cross-allergy; senior doctor decision after discussion with anaesthesia: cefuroxime acceptable with caution for a pure amoxicillin/urticaria reaction, no anaphylaxis risk according to the allergy protocol).

Keep metamizole for pain until surgery.

P003-D009.title: Anaesthesia record – laparoscopic appendectomy
P003-D009.text:
Anaesthesia record, 09.07.2024
Patient: Gruber Sabine, born 14.02.1993
Procedure: laparoscopic appendectomy (emergency)
Anaesthetist: Dr Norbert Gasser

Short pre-operative visit:
ASA II (bronchial asthma, well controlled). No current exacerbation, SpO2 99%.
Allergies: penicillin (urticaria)! Cephalosporin prophylaxis OK per senior doctor decision.
Airway: Mallampati I, no dentures.

Induction: propofol 180 mg IV, fentanyl 0.1 mg, rocuronium 50 mg.
Airway: video laryngoscope intubation (precaution for asthma), tube 7.0 without problems.
Sugammadex 200 mg for reversal at the end of surgery.

During surgery: stable vital signs. SpO2 99%. No bronchospasm.
Duration: 55 minutes.
Blood loss: minimal (<50 ml).

Problems: none.
Recovery room: woke up without problems, SpO2 99%, no bronchospasm.

P003-D010.title: Surgery report: laparoscopic appendectomy
P003-D010.text:
Surgery report
Date: 09.07.2024, 02:15–03:10
Surgeon: Senior Dr Franz Kern
Assistant: Dr Tobias Winkler
Anaesthesia: Dr N. Gasser (general anaesthesia)

Diagnosis: acute appendicitis (K37)

Indication: acute appendicitis confirmed clinically, by lab and by ultrasound. Free fluid around the appendix on ultrasound → surgery indicated.

Procedure: supine position. Disinfection, sterile draping. Three-trocar technique (umbilicus 10 mm, right lower abdomen 5 mm, left lower abdomen 5 mm). CO2 pneumoperitoneum, pressure 12 mmHg. Inspection of the abdomen:
- Appendix: inflamed, diameter about 10 mm, fibrin coating, NO perforation. Small amount of clear fluid around the appendix.
- Left ovary: follicular cyst about 2.5 cm, calm, no intervention needed.
- Rest of the abdomen: normal.

Appendectomy: mesoappendix coagulated and divided with LigaSure. Appendix base secured with Endoloop (2×). Appendix removed in a retrieval bag. Irrigation with NaCl 0.9% (500 ml). No sign of peritonitis.

Haemostasis: achieved. Trocar wounds: fascia of the 10 mm trocar closed with PDS 0, skin intracutaneous suture and metal staples.

Finding during surgery: acute phlegmonous appendicitis, not perforated.

Histology: appendix sent for histology.

Complications: none during surgery.

Post-operative orders:
- Stop metamizole → paracetamol 1 g IV/orally every 6 h (better GI tolerance)
- Cefuroxime 1.5 g IV once after surgery (prophylaxis then finished)
- Start eating from tomorrow morning
- Continue inhaler therapy (budesonide/formoterol and salbutamol as needed)
- Await histology result

P003-D011.title: Progress note, day 1 after surgery
P003-D011.text:
09.07.2024, 09:00, Dr T. Winkler
Day 1 after laparoscopic appendectomy.

Patient awake, oriented, good general condition. Abdominal pain NRS 2/10 on paracetamol.
Temp 37.4°C. BP 112/68, pulse 80/min. SpO2 99%.
Abdomen: soft, slightly tender around the navel, bowel sounds back.
Right shoulder pain from the pneumoperitoneum: decreasing.
Laparoscopy sites: calm, dry.
Lungs: vesicular both sides, no crackles. No bronchospasm.

Diet: drinking without problems, soft diet started.
Inhaler: budesonide/formoterol given, good technique.

Lab (09.07., 07:00):
  Hb 12.8 g/dl, leucocytes 10.4 G/l (falling), CRP 62 mg/l (expected reactive rise after surgery).

Plan:
- Build up diet
- Discharge tomorrow if all well
- Gynaecology consult requested for the left ovarian cyst

P003-D012.title: Gynaecology consultation – left ovarian cyst
P003-D012.text:
Gynaecology consultation report, 09.07.2024
Consultant: Dr Eva Steinbauer, gynaecology

Reason: hypoechoic lesion of the left ovary, about 2.5 cm, described on ultrasound and during surgery.

Findings:
Gynaecological examination: normal. Transvaginal ultrasound (TVUS): left ovary: hypoechoic, thin-walled, smoothly outlined structure about 2.4 cm, no internal echoes, no septum → morphologically a clear follicular cyst.
Right ovary: normal.
Uterus: normal.

Assessment: morphologically benign follicular cyst on the left, no sign of ovarian cancer or endometriosis. No intervention needed.
Recommendation: TVUS check after the next period (about 4–6 weeks). Follicular cysts usually resolve on their own.

Diagnosis: follicular cyst of the left ovary – no surgery needed.

P003-D013.title: Progress note day 2 – preparing discharge
P003-D013.text:
10.07.2024, 08:30, Dr Winkler
Day 2 after surgery, preparing discharge.

No symptoms, good general condition. Pain 0–1/10 on oral paracetamol.
Temp 36.8°C, no fever. Pulse 72/min, BP 110/66.
Wounds: calm. Metal staples in place (to be removed by the GP in 7–10 days).
Diet: normal, eats well.
Lungs: clear.

Gynaecology consult: follicular cyst – no intervention, outpatient check.

Discharge planned today.
Discharge letter being prepared.

Allergy note: penicillin allergy correctly recorded in the patient file (admission report wrongly said "no known allergies" – corrected).

P003-D014.title: Discharge letter after appendectomy
P003-D014.text:
Discharge letter
Musterstadt Regional Hospital, General Surgery
Date: 10.07.2024

Dear colleagues,

We are discharging Mrs Sabine Gruber, born 14.02.1993, after an inpatient stay from 08.07.2024 to 10.07.2024.

Main diagnoses:
1. Acute phlegmonous appendicitis, not perforated (K37)
2. Status after laparoscopic appendectomy (09.07.2024)
3. Bronchial asthma (J45.0) – known, no complications around surgery

Secondary diagnoses:
4. Follicular cyst of the left ovary (N83.0) – no action needed, outpatient check

Course:
Admitted on 08.07.2024 with acute lower abdominal pain. Lab and ultrasound consistent with acute appendicitis. Laparoscopic appendectomy in the night to 09.07.2024, not perforated during surgery (ultrasound had not safely excluded perforation). Uneventful course after surgery. Gynaecology consult for the left follicular cyst – no intervention needed.

Allergies: CAUTION penicillin allergy (urticaria after amoxicillin as a child, confirmed by the children's hospital report 2009). The admission report wrongly recorded "no known allergies" – discovered by a nurse during the night and corrected.

Medication at discharge:
1. Budesonide/formoterol 160/4.5 µg (Symbicort) inhaled twice daily – asthma (unchanged)
2. Salbutamol 100 µg (Ventolin) inhaled as needed – asthma emergency medication (unchanged)
3. Paracetamol 500 mg as needed (max. 4x/day) – pain relief for 5 days

Recommendations:
- Staple removal by the GP in 7–10 days
- Gynaecology check (TVUS) in 4–6 weeks
- Pulmonology: next routine asthma check as planned
- Avoid physical strain for 2 weeks

Kind regards, Senior Dr Franz Kern, general surgery
Musterstadt Regional Hospital
